name: Mathematics and Statistics
notes: Fourteen courses: eleven foundational or core, three additional advanced. Approval of advisors in BOTH mathematics and statistics is required.
Equivalent substitutions: MATH 163 or MATH 173 for MATH 165; MATH 171/172/174 for MATH 161/162/164; MATH 141-143 for MATH 161-162. AP courses may satisfy foundational requirements.
Advanced courses are mathematics courses numbered 200+ (excluding 500+) and statistics courses numbered 214 and higher.
Beyond STAT 226W the second writing course may be a STAT W course, MATH 391W (one credit, taken alongside another course), or an approved 4-credit ULW course in another department.

requirementGroups.label: Foundational mathematics
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: The following foundational courses must be completed before acceptance into the major: MATH 161; MATH 162; MATH 164; MATH 165

requirementGroups.label: Core courses
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: MATH/STAT 201: Introduction to Probability; MATH/STAT 203: Introduction to Mathematical Statistics; MATH/STAT 208: Operations Research I; STAT 226W: Introduction to Linear Models; MATH 265: Functions of a Real Variable I

requirementGroups.label: Linear algebra
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: MATH 235: Linear Algebra or MATH 173: Honors Calculus III

requirementGroups.label: Computing
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: CSC 161 or 171. Equivalent classes also accepted when approved by the statistics program advisor.

requirementGroups.label: Advanced mathematics or statistics (3)
requirementGroups.sourceQuote: Students must complete three 4-credit advanced courses in mathematics or statistics. Advanced courses are math classes numbered 200 or higher (excluding 500+ level) and stat classes numbered 214 and higher.

upperLevelWriting.label: STAT 226W plus one more writing course
upperLevelWriting.sourceQuote: In addition to STAT 226W, students must pass one more writing course, to be chosen from the following options: A statistics course with the W designation; MATH 391W; A four credit course, approved in advance, satisfying part of the upper level writing requirement in another department
